summary: Daito Shimaji (1875–1927) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Ryukoku University (1893) and Toyo University (1897), and later taught at Toyo (~1903), Komazawa (~1904), Rissho (~1904), and the University of Tokyo (1923).

Dale S. Wright (born 1948) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Alan Anderson, Wei Pachow (~1976–1980), and Robert Scharlemann (~1976–1980), and became Professor of Religious Studies and Asian Studies at Occidental College (~1980).

Dalsukh D. Malvania (1910–2000) was an Indologist and scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under Sukhlal Sanghvi. He held posts at Banaras Hindu University (attested 1951) and served as Director of the Lalbhai Dalpatbhai Institute of Indology (attested 1965–1971).
Damchö Gyatso is a scholar who studied under Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse, Penor Rinpoche, and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.
Damdin Badaraev worked in Tibetology and linguistics, having studied under Bidia Dandaron and George de Roerich.

Damien Keown (born 1951) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy who founded the Journal of Buddhist Ethics. He earned a B.A. from Lancaster University (~1974–1977), a D.Phil. from Oxford (~1981–1986), and taught at Goldsmiths, University of London (~1987).

Damodar Dharmananda Kosambi (1907–1966) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Harvard under George David Birkhoff, and held posts at Banaras Hindu University, Aligarh Muslim University, Fergusson College, the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, and the University of Chicago.

Dan Arnold (born 1965), a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology, studied at Carleton, Columbia, Iliff, and the University of Chicago (PhD ~1997–2003). He served on the faculties of McGill University (2003–2004) and the University of Chicago Divinity School (2004–2011).

Dan Lusthaus (born 1950) specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy and earned his Ph.D. at Temple University. He held positions at Grinnell, Florida State, the University of Georgia, and Harvard, and also taught at UCLA, UIUC, Boston University, and Bates.

Dan Martin (born 1953) is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. at Indiana University (~1984–1991) under Elliot Sperling and others. He has been affiliated with the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters and Hebrew University of Jerusalem.

Dan Smyer Yü specializes in religious studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of California, Davis, and served as a Research Group Leader at the Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity.

Dan Zahavi (born 1967) is a philosopher who earned his PhD at KU Leuven under Rudolf Bernet and his Dr.phil. at the University of Copenhagen. He has held professorships at the University of Copenhagen (2002) and the University of Oxford (2018–2021).

Daniel A. Getz specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology, completing his Ph.D. at Yale University (attested 1994) under Stanley Weinstein, Ying-shih Yü, Masaaki Chikusa, and Taryo Makita. He became an associate professor at Bradley University (attested 2019).
Daniel Amadé Scheidegger is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies who completed his doctoral degree at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Paul Williams.

Daniel B. Stevenson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his Ph.D. from Columbia University. He held assistant professorships at Butler University (attested 1986) and the University of Kansas (attested 1996–2003), and was a guest scholar at Soka University.
Daniel Borengasser is a scholar in Japanology and history/archaeology. He completed his Master of Arts at the University of Oregon under the supervision of Akiko Walley (attested 2014).

Daniel Boucher specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Indiana University and earned his doctorate at the University of Pennsylvania (-1996) under Victor H. Mair, later serving as an associate professor at Cornell University (attested 2000–2008).

Daniel Clarke Waugh is a historian of Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Yale (B.A. 1963) and Harvard (Master's 1965, doctorate 1972) before joining the faculty of the University of Washington in 1972.

Daniel Coit Gilman (1831–1908) studied at Yale, Harvard, Cambridge, and Berlin. He served as librarian at Yale (1856–1872), president of the University of California (1872–1875), founding president of Johns Hopkins (1875–1901), and president of the Carnegie Institution (1902–1904).

Daniel Cozort (born 1953) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia (~1980–1989) under Jeffrey Hopkins. He held posts at Bates College (~1987–1988) and Dickinson College (~1988).
